html:
The Persian Constitutional Revolution was a movement in Iran from 1905 to 1911 that forced the Qajar shah to accept a constitution and an elected parliament, the Majlis.

Anger had built over foreign concessions, debts to Europe and the shah's spending. Merchants of the bazaar, Shia clerics and reformers joined forces. In 1906 thousands took sanctuary in the British legation grounds in Tehran, and Mozaffar ad-Din Shah gave way. The first Majlis met that year and wrote a constitution.

His successor Mohammad Ali Shah shelled the parliament in 1908 with the help of the Russian-led Cossack Brigade. Constitutionalist fighters from Tabriz and the Bakhtiari tribes took Tehran in 1909 and deposed him.

Britain and Russia had already split Iran into zones of influence in 1907. In 1911 Russian troops forced the Majlis to dismiss its American treasurer, Morgan Shuster, and the revolution ended. It was the first such movement in the region after the Ottoman constitution, and its ideas returned in later Iranian struggles.
sum: The Persian Constitutional Revolution was a movement in Iran from 1905 to 1911 that forced the Qajar shah to accept a constitution and an elected parliament, the Majlis.
